• “What Brands Get Wrong About Sports Sponsorships—and How to Get Them Right” | Human creativity still beats AI in many advertising contexts; brands should focus on authenticity and real customer insights. | | **Product & Design** | • “What the Honda Super Cub Can Teach Us About Designing for Global Markets” | Simple, adaptable product design can unlock new global opportunities. | ### What you’ll get from the page - **Concise, actionable insights** – Most pieces are a few paragraphs long, perfect for quick reading during a commute or break. - **Diverse perspectives** – Articles come from a range of experts (Liz Fosslien, Kim Scott, Nitin Nohria, etc.) covering everything from AI strategy to work‑life balance. - **Practical tools** – Several posts provide “How‑to” steps, such as mapping AI workflows for product development or setting up productive conflict in your team. - **Supplementary media** – Alongside written pieces, there are audio podcasts and sponsor webinars (e.g., AWS + Arize on agentic AI) to broaden learning options. ### Bottom line Harvard Business Review’s “Ideas and Advice for Leaders” page serves as a quick‑reference library for executives looking to: - Leverage AI responsibly while keeping people at the center. - Strengthen cybersecurity through trust and smart policy. - Foster healthy team dynamics and effective delegation. - Make strategic decisions that blend human judgment with AI insights. If you’re a busy leader, this page gives you bite‑sized wisdom you can apply right away—whether you’re revamping your company’s AI strategy, tightening up cybersecurity, or simply looking for better ways to motivate your team.
